questions.stem: Which two characteristics define cloud services as a replacement for on-premises infrastructure?

choices.text: Always-cheaper pricing and zero security responsibility
Scalability (add resources on demand) and high availability (redundancy/backups)
Single-tenant hardware and no internet dependency
Mandatory on-prem mirror copies and offline-only operation

questions.explanation: Cloud's defining traits per the transcript are scalability (resources on demand) and high availability via built-in redundancy and backups.
questions.trap: Cloud is not automatically cheaper, and the customer still has security responsibilities under the shared-responsibility model.

questions.stem: A laptop has limited disk space. The user wants OneDrive files visible in File Explorer but only downloaded when actually opened. Which sync mode fits?

choices.text: Mirror (everything stored locally)
Selective sync of only a few folders
Cloud-only files (placeholders downloaded on demand)
Disable OneDrive entirely

questions.explanation: Cloud-only mode keeps files visible but downloads on demand, preserving local disk space - the right answer for a low-storage laptop.
questions.trap: Selective sync helps, but it hides folders entirely; the user wanted visibility plus on-demand download.

questions.stem: Which trio of services are examples of identity synchronization platforms that create one central user identity across cloud apps?

choices.text: Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google Identity
OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox
Outlook, Gmail, Apple Mail
Teams, Slack, Zoom

questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, and Google Identity are the identity-sync platforms named in the transcript - the single source of truth for a user's identity across cloud apps.
questions.trap: OneDrive/Google Drive/Dropbox are storage; Teams/Slack/Zoom are collaboration. Identity sync is a separate layer.

questions.stem: An employee leaves the company. The admin disables the user in the central identity directory. What happens?

choices.text: Nothing - each cloud app must also be disabled individually
Only email is affected; other apps continue to work
Their data is permanently deleted from every app
The user immediately loses access to ALL connected cloud services

questions.explanation: Identity sync gives a single global access badge. Disabling the user centrally cuts access to every connected service immediately.
questions.trap: Without identity sync the admin WOULD have to disable per app; the value of identity sync is centralized revocation.

questions.stem: Why is centralized license assignment in cloud productivity suites efficient and cost-effective?

choices.text: Licenses are physical USB keys mailed to each user
Admins can view the license pool and instantly assign, revoke, or reassign licenses from one cloud console
Licenses cannot be reassigned once issued
Each license is tied to a specific physical PC

questions.explanation: Cloud license assignment is centrally managed. Admins can view the full pool and instantly assign, revoke, or reassign a license, so the company never pays for unused seats.
questions.trap: Physical keys / device-bound licensing are old on-prem models; the cloud model is dynamic reassignment.

questions.stem: Which on-premises system is most directly replaced by cloud platforms like Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace?

choices.text: Local Exchange or mail servers
Domain controllers
Print servers
Patch management appliances

questions.explanation: M365 and Google Workspace primarily replace local Exchange / mail servers and on-prem productivity infrastructure.
questions.trap: Cloud directories (Entra ID) are related but distinct from M365/Workspace as a productivity suite.

questions.stem: A team of three is editing the same spreadsheet at the same time and seeing each other's edits in real time. Which cloud capability makes this possible?

choices.text: Identity synchronization
Selective sync
Real-time co-authoring in shared cloud documents
License assignment

questions.explanation: Real-time co-authoring of shared docs/sheets is the cloud collaboration feature that lets multiple users edit simultaneously.
questions.trap: Identity sync handles WHO is allowed in, not the collaborative editing itself.

questions.stem: OneDrive client sync is configured to 'mirror everything locally'. What is the trade-off?

choices.text: Lowest local disk usage but slowest file access
Same disk usage as cloud-only mode
It disables cloud backup completely
Highest local disk usage and fastest offline access

questions.explanation: Mirror mode keeps a complete local copy of everything. That uses the most disk but provides the fastest offline access.
questions.trap: Cloud-only is the disk-saving option; mirror is the opposite trade-off.
